If the rejection is carried onto the PWU's own assurance axis, satisfaction is blocked PERMANENTLY: PWU.assuranceState REJECTED has ZERO out-arrows (derived from getMachine, not read), so REJECTED->SATISFIED is not on the matrix and the only in-arrow to workLifecycle SATISFIED requires assuranceState === 'SATISFIED'. So in that arrangement the refusal genuinely keys on a rejected mandatory assessment.

WHAT DEFEATS IT: NOTHING PERFORMS THE ROLLUP. `completeAssuranceAssessment` returning REJECTED writes the ASSESSMENT aggregate and does not touch the PWU's axes — measured, not read: after the REJECTED completion the PWU walked UNASSESSED -> EVIDENCE_REQUIRED -> READY_FOR_ASSESSMENT -> ASSESSING -> SATISFIED unimpeded, with the rejected assessment still reading REJECTED at the end. The quantifier 'ANY rejected mandatory assessment' is the whole rule and the engine has no reader for the set: the controller supplies `supportingObjectIds`, `rejectUnbackedDisposition` validates THOSE with `cited.some(...)`, and an assessment sitting REJECTED against a policy the PWU's own `assurancePolicyIds` names is never loaded. So the rule holds only when the professional volunteers the very fact the rule exists to force.

evidence:
WHAT THE LIMB FORBIDS: a mandatory parent obligation whose fate is not one of FOUR named classes — allocated to children, retained by parent, already satisfied, explicitly waived/superseded by valid authority. It is an EQUATION, so it is only 'the thing being checked' if all four terms are expressible and counted.

WHAT THE CODE DOES. `validateObligationConservation` (packages/rph-domain/src/decomposition.ts:62-84) unions exactly four sets — `allocated ∪ retained ∪ satisfied ∪ waived` (:65-68, :76-79) — over parent obligations whose `strength === 'MANDATORY'` (:74), and emits MISSING_OBLIGATION_ALLOCATION for any with none (:82). `buildObligationInput` (packages/rph-application/src/handlers/decomposition.ts:146-172) is the ONLY production site that fills those four sets. TERM BY TERM, AS THAT BUILDER SUPPLIES THEM:

  TERM 1, 'allocated to children' — DIVERGENT, DRIVEN, UNFILED. decomposition.ts:168 reads `allocatedObligationIds: [...allocations.map((a) => a.obligationId), ...objAllocated]`. It maps the allocation record to its `obligationId` and DISCARDS `allocatedTo`. `ObligationAllocationSchema` is `{ obligationId, allocatedTo: string[] }` (packages/rph-contracts/src/objects.ts:306-309), so the field naming the children EXISTS on the wire and no predicate at this site reads it. DRIVEN: a decomposition whose only disposition of a MANDATORY obligation is `{obligationId: OBL, allocatedTo: []}` — allocated to NOBODY — was marked VALID; and one allocating to a PWU that is not among `childWorkUnitIds` was also marked VALID. The engine's OWN oracle takes the opposite reading over the same field: packages/rph-engine/src/graph-conformance.ts:105-107 counts an obligation unallocated when `!targets || targets.length === 0 || !targets.every((t) => children.has(t))`, with the comment 'Allocated to NOTHING, or to something that is not a child of this decomposition, is not allocation.' Two committed sites, one field, opposite answers — and the command gate uses the weaker one.

  TERM 2, 'retained by parent' — LIVE AND CHECKED. decomposition.ts:169 reads the contract's `retainedParentObligationIds`. CONTROL 1 (identical decomposition, obligation retained) was ACCEPTED and the contract reached VALID, which is what proves the refusal in PROBE 1 discriminates rather than fires for everything.

  TERM 3, 'already satisfied' — UNREACHABLE. decomposition.ts:170 sources it ONLY from `satisfiedObligationIds: objSatisfied`, and `objSatisfied` is filled at :162 by `else if (status === 'SATISFIED')` on the OBLIGATION object. `Obligation.status` can never hold that value: the only OBLIGATION command mints at PROPOSED (packages/rph-application/src/handlers/obligation-constraint.ts:34, births declared at :39) and no handler advances the machine. DRIVEN: after five dispatch attempts the obligation still read PROPOSED.

  TERM 4, 'explicitly waived/superseded by valid authority' — UNREACHABLE, AND 'valid authority' IS NEVER CONSULTED EVEN IF IT WERE. `authorizedWaiverObligationIds: objWaived` (:171) is filled at :163 by `else if (status === 'WAIVED')`; the 'superseded' half is the `continue` at :159 on `status === 'SUPERSEDED'`. Both statuses are unreachable by the same census. No Decision, waiver object or authority reference is loaded on this path (contrast `buildConstraintInput`'s `authorityBasis` at :250-256, which DOES resolve a DECISION — the obligation half has no counterpart).

SO THE EQUATION THE ENGINE CHECKS IS A TWO-TERM ONE: `allocated(a record mentioning the id, holder unread) ∪ retained`. Two of canon's four classes cannot be put on the wire at all, and the first class is credited without its 'to children' qualifier.

The mechanism is at the cited site: collectConstraintFindings (rph-domain/src/decomposition.ts:186) groups records into a LIST per constraintId, folds their children into a `covered` SET (so N records naming one child collapse to a single 'covered' mark), then runs the per-record well-formedness loop at :208. Neither structure can see MULTIPLICITY: nothing anywhere counts dispositions per (constraint, child) pair. A second, weaker arrangement is also admitted (S13): PROPAGATED[A,B] + INAPPLICABLE[A,B] was refused only because the INAPPLICABLE record lacked an authority — i.e. the refusal was about that record's well-formedness, never about the contradiction. (b) 'retaining ... STRENGTH' — inexpressible: `propagatedStrength` (and a bare `strength`) on a propagation record is refused by ConstraintPropagationSchema's z.strictObject before any handler runs. So a propagation cannot declare it keeps MANDATORY, and the kernel arm that would check it (decomposition.ts:221, CONSTRAINT_WEAKENED_WITHOUT_AUTHORITY) is a dead predicate. (c) 'retaining AUTHORITY' — the propagation record carries no authority field, and more sharply the propagation never reaches the child at all: after ValidateDecomposition marked the contract VALID on a clean PROPAGATED[A,B], CHILD_A.constraintIds and CHILD_B.constraintIds were both [] and the CONSTRAINT object was still sitting on the parent at MANDATORY/PROPOSED. `state.constraintPropagations` is read at exactly ONE site in production — the validation gate itself (handlers/decomposition.ts:250) — so 'propagated' is a bookkeeping claim on the contract with no downstream carrier of authority or strength.

evidence:
THE LIMB IS A CONJUNCTION AND THE TWO CONJUNCTS COME OUT DIFFERENTLY.

CONJUNCT (a) 'references an active policy version' — ENFORCED, and I drove it. `requestAssuranceAssessment` loads the cited ASSURANCE_POLICY and fails closed twice: once when it does not exist, once when `policy.status !== 'ACTIVE'`. A DRAFT policy is REJECTED with RPH_VALIDATION_SEMANTIC_FAILED; the byte-identical request against the SAME policy after ActivateAssurancePolicy is ACCEPTED. This binds a VERSION and not merely a policy, because a policy version is its own aggregate here: `version` is set once at CreateAssurancePolicy and is absent from EditAssurancePolicyPayloadSchema (messages.ts:712-731), and a successor is a distinct policyId reached via SupersedeAssurancePolicy — so the DRAFT/SUSPENDED/SUPERSEDED status test IS the not-active-version test.

CONJUNCT (b) 'and its subject's exact semantic version' — ADMITTED at BOTH moments, driven. (i) At request: the PWU is at semanticVersion 1 and `subjectSemanticVersions: {pwu: 99}` is ACCEPTED and stored verbatim; `{}` (no version at all for a named subject) is ACCEPTED at request too. (ii) At completion: a validatorResult declaring the subject at v7 while the PWU is at v1 is ACCEPTED, the assessment advances to SATISFIED, and the emitted AssuranceAssessmentCompleted payload records subjectSemanticVersions {pwu: 7} — a SATISFIED verdict in the audit log for a version the subject has never been at.

WHY THE ONE CHECK THAT DOES READ THE FIELD IS NOT THIS. `parseCompletion` (assurance.ts:1818-1830) refuses a completion whose `subjectObjectIds` names a subject with no numeric entry in `subjectSemanticVersions`. That is a COMPLETENESS test (is a version NAMED) and is RPH-ASR-007's ENFORCED limb; it keys on presence, never on equality with the subject. I drove it as the control precisely so the two refusals could be told apart: the SAME command with `{}` is REJECTED at the SAME site while the wrong-number version sails through.

CENSUS OF THE ABSENCE, checked in both directions. Exactly TWO production sites anywhere compare a recorded assessment version against a live subject version, and NEITHER is on the assessment command path: floor-gate.ts:314 (`rec?.version === opts.subjectVersion`) and the pure kernel floor.ts:320 (`r.subjectSemanticVersion === subject.semanticVersion`). Inside handlers/assurance.ts there are ZERO such comparisons against 10 mentions of the field.

evidence:
ENFORCED AT THE FLOOR GATE, ADMITTED ON THE PWU SATISFACTION PLANE. Both halves driven.

ENFORCED HALF. `floorGateBlock` computes `versionOk = rec?.version === opts.subjectVersion`, where `rec.version` is THE SUBJECT VERSION THE RECORDED ASSESSMENT BOUND (latestFloorDispositions reads `s.subjectSemanticVersions?.[subjectId]` off the stored ASSURANCE_ASSESSMENT, floor-gate.ts:245) and `opts.subjectVersion` is THE SUBJECT'S LIVE VERSION READ FROM THE LOADED AGGREGATE (`const version = Number(state.semanticVersion ?? 1);`, pwa-authoring.ts:965). A version-mismatched assessment is downgraded to MISSING and the protected transition is refused. Two live callers: publishPwa via pwaFloorGate (pwa-authoring.ts:966) and completeExecutionStep over each step-output subject (execution.ts:1432).

I RAN THE LANE'S OWN ASR-15:5 TRAP CHECK ON IT — does the predicate read the SUBJECT, or only the payload? It reads the SUBJECT, and I proved it by MOVING the subject rather than forging a number. The floor was recorded SATISFIED at PWA v2; two real authoring commands (DefinePwuType + EditPwuType) then raised the PWA to v4; the identical PublishPwa was REJECTED. The three assessments were byte-identical in probe and control; the only thing that changed was the world. CONTROL: the same drive with the post-floor edit omitted publishes cleanly (ACCEPTED, publicationStatus PUBLISHED), so the refusal discriminates on exactly the relation the limb names and on nothing else.

ADMITTED HALF. `rejectUnbackedDisposition` (pwu.ts:1350-1378) is the guard on ChangePwuState -> assuranceState SATISFIED. It loads each cited object and tests TWO of its fields — `s.assessmentState === p.assuranceState` and `(s.subjectObjectIds ?? []).includes(id)` — and never touches `subjectSemanticVersions`, and never loads the PWU's own semanticVersion. Driven: an assessment REQUESTED and COMPLETED SATISFIED with pin {pwu: 0} — an assessment of version 0 — satisfies a PWU sitting at semanticVersion 1. ACCEPTED, and the PWU's assuranceState really becomes SATISFIED. That is n satisfying n+1, from a true premise, with no forgery anywhere in the arrangement.

SO THE UNION OF THE ENFORCING SITES IS NOT TOTAL, which is why this is not ENFORCED_MULTI_SITE: the version binding is consulted at PWA publication and at execution-step-output completion, and nowhere on the path by which an assessment actually satisfies a work unit.

sibling_control:
WHAT floor-gate.ts:314 REFUSES IN ITS OWN TERMS: 'at a protected transition over subject S, a recorded floor assessment whose BOUND subject semanticVersion differs from S's CURRENT semanticVersion does not count as SATISFIED'. Word by word against the limb: same two operands (an assessment's version, the subject's version), same relation (n vs n+1), same consequent (does not satisfy). Not a sibling.

TWO NEAR NEIGHBOURS RULED OUT. (1) `decisionAuthorizesVersions` (rph-domain/src/governance.ts:100), cited by register row RPH-GOV-003, quantifies over DECISIONS — canon ASR-15:5, 'a decision approving version n never authorizes version n+1'. Different object class, and its operand is a DECISION's pin; citing it here would be the exact EM-1 the lane brief warned about. (2) `rejectUnauthorizedWaiver` (pwu.ts, refusal text "whose subjectSemanticVersions pin ${id} at ${currentSemanticVersion}") DOES compare a cited object's pin against the PWU's live semanticVersion — but the cited object is an EFFECTIVE decisionType=WAIVER DECISION, i.e. ASR-14/ASR-15. It sits in the SAME handler three lines from rejectUnbackedDisposition and reads the subject's version the way the assessment guard does not, which is what makes the assessment gap a MISSING LIMB rather than a dead site.

AND I RECORD THE TENSION WITH THE REGISTER RATHER THAN HIDING IT: RPH-ASR-010's note says "WHY THE FLOOR GATE IS NOT THIS RULE. Its subject is a PWA at publication ... this rule's subject is an assessment of a work unit at satisfaction time." That is right about the RATIFIED statement, whose subject is scoped. Canon ASR-12 scopes no subject, so the floor gate IS a partial enforcement site of the canon limb — which is exactly why this row is PARTIAL and not UNENFORCED.

Nothing in `canPromoteBaseline` performs a set comparison: `findVersionMismatches` (packages/rph-domain/src/governance.ts:277-292) iterates `candidateItems` ONLY, so a candidate array that DROPS items produces no finding even in principle, and `findMissingItemVersions` (:263-275) fires only on `undefined`/`null` — values `PromoteBaselinePayloadSchema` (packages/rph-contracts/src/messages.ts:239-245, `semanticVersion: z.number().int()`) has already made unreachable, i.e. a schema-foreclosed arm, so MISSING_ITEM_VERSION cannot appear in any dispatch result. WHAT IS HELD, stated so this row is not read as stronger than it is: the payload SHAPE is schema-closed — omitting the item's `semanticVersion`, omitting `expectedItemObjectVersions`, omitting `promotionDecisionId` and adding an undeclared key are all VALIDATION_FAILED (S5a-d). evidence:
WHAT THE LIMB FORBIDS. "A command expresses a requested mutation and may fail" is a claim about the KIND: a command is a REQUEST (not a fact), and fallibility is not optional for any of them. The arrangement it forbids is a command that is treated as already-accepted, or a command type exempt from the possibility of refusal. THE ARM IS BY CONSTRUCTION BECAUSE BOTH HALVES ARE INEXPRESSIBLE, AND I MEASURED BOTH OVER THE WHOLE POPULATION RATHER THAN AT ONE SITE.

(a) COMMAND AND EVENT ARE DISJOINT KINDS ON THE WIRE, WITH DISJOINT NAMESPACES. `DomainCommandSchema` (packages/rph-contracts/src/envelopes.ts, `domainCommandSchema`) and `DomainEventSchema` (`domainEventSchema`) are two separate `z.strictObject`s with non-overlapping required fields (`commandId/commandType/commandSchemaVersion/targetAggregateType/targetAggregateId/idempotencyKey` vs `eventId/eventType/eventSchemaVersion/aggregateType/aggregateId/aggregateRevision/actor`). The dispatch surface returns `CommandResultSchema` — `z.strictObject({commandId, status, producedEventIds, error?})` — and NEVER a DomainEvent; I confirmed the returned object's own key set at runtime: `["commandId","producedEventIds","status"]`. Driven: submitting an EVENT TYPE on the command wire (`dispatch('PwuProposed', …)`) is refused verbatim `REJECTED / RPH_VALIDATION_SCHEMA_FAILED / Unknown command type: PwuProposed`, while the corresponding real command `ProposePwu` with the same payload is ACCEPTED. evidence: WHAT THE LIMB FORBIDS: a command whose declared revision conflicts with the aggregate's current revision being applied. THE SITE: `loadOrReject`, packages/rph-application/src/handlers/kit.ts:144 `if (command.expectedRevision !== undefined && command.expectedRevision !== existing.revision)` -> `reject(command, 'RPH_REVISION_CONFLICT', `Revision conflict on ${id}: command expected revision ${command.expectedRevision}, actual is ${existing.revision}`, [id])`, with `STATUS_FOR_CODE` (kit.ts:93) mapping the code to CommandResult status CONFLICT. I DROVE THE TRUE STALE-READ ARRANGEMENT, not merely a wrong number: caller A read the INTENT at revision 0 and formed intent against that read; a concurrent writer ran BeginIntentDiscovery, moving it to revision 1; caller A then dispatched ProvisionIntent carrying its stale expectedRevision=0. REFUSED, and the aggregate did not move — revision stayed 1, lifecycleStatus stayed UNDER_DISCOVERY, and the event stream stayed ["0:IntentCaptured","1:IntentDiscoveryStarted"] with NO third event. That last check matters for the canon wording: canon says "the command is rejected" and the CommandResult status is CONFLICT rather than REJECTED, so I verified the substance PER-1 defines rejection by — "Command rejection produces a command result, never a domain event" — zero events appended. CONFLICT is the ratified refusal shape for this code, not a downgrade: packages/rph-domain/src/enforcement-register.ts:3961 `DECLARABLE_REFUSAL_STATUSES = ['CONFLICT', 'UNAUTHORIZED']`, and RPH-PER-001 declares `refusalStatus: 'CONFLICT'` with a recorded mutant proving that field load-bearing (dropping RPH_REVISION_CONFLICT from STATUS_FOR_CODE leaves code and message intact and changes only the status — "a register reading code and marker alone would have called it a kill"). SINGLE SITE, AND I CHECKED THAT IT IS TOTAL rather than assuming it: every production UPDATE path funnels through `loadOrReject` (20 production call sites) before `commitState`, and the census of what those paths hand to `commitState` shows 19 `expectedRevision:` arguments of which 16 are `loaded.revision` (i.e. post-loadOrReject) and exactly 3 are `undefined` — intent.ts:82, kit.ts:667 (`createObject`), pwu.ts:370 — all three being CREATE paths, which canon's NON-EXAMPLE exempts. So there is no update handler that reaches the store without passing this check, which is why this is ENFORCED_DRIVEN and not ENFORCED_MULTI_SITE. THE SECOND, DEEPER GUARD IS NAMED AND EXPLICITLY NOT RELIED ON: `commitState` (kit.ts:529 -> :538) maps a failed `ctx.store.commit` to the same code with a DIFFERENT message ('Revision conflict on X (actual revision N)'). It cannot fire sequentially — `commitState` hands the store the revision it just loaded, so expected always equals actual — which REG-F-050 records ("the protection that exists is unreachable") and RPH-PER-001's own declaredMutations confirm by observation. This row therefore rests on the handler arm alone, which is also the arm that sees the CLIENT's declared expectation, i.e. the limb's actual subject.

evidence: THE LIMB IS A CLAIM ABOUT THE CALLER, AND I TREATED THAT AS A QUESTION TO SETTLE BY MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN AS A REASON TO EXCUSE THE ENGINE. The decisive test is whether the engine can DISTINGUISH a caller that reloaded current state and re-formed intent from one that took the refusal's number and bumped it. I drove both, in one process, against identical aggregates. FORBIDDEN ARRANGEMENT: caller A read the INTENT at revision 0 (RAW) and formed the payload object `{ambiguityIds: []}` against that read; a concurrent writer ran BeginIntentDiscovery -> revision 1 (UNDER_DISCOVERY); caller A dispatched ProvisionIntent at expectedRevision=0 and was correctly refused with RPH_REVISION_CONFLICT; caller A then resubmitted THE SAME payload object — never reloading, never re-reading state, never re-deciding — with expectedRevision bumped to believed+1. ACCEPTED. CONTROL (the arrangement canon prescribes): a second aggregate driven through the identical concurrent write, where caller A then calls loadObject, sees revision 1 / UNDER_DISCOVERY, and dispatches against the reload. ALSO ACCEPTED. THE TWO RUNS PRODUCE BYTE-IDENTICAL AGGREGATE STREAMS — [0,1,2] and [0,1,2], same event types, same revisions, same final PROVISIONAL state. There is nothing in the record that differs, which is what "no shape" means concretely: the engine did not fail to check, it has nothing to check against. WHY THIS IS NOT UNENFORCED_DEAD_PREDICATE: a dead predicate needs a predicate. There is no branch anywhere that reads read-provenance, because no field carries it. The command envelope (packages/rph-contracts/src/envelopes.ts:100+, `domainCommandSchema`) is commandId / commandType / commandSchemaVersion / targetAggregateType / targetAggregateId / expectedRevision / issuedAt / issuedBy? / correlationId / causationId? / idempotencyKey / payload. `expectedRevision` records a NUMBER the caller asserts; nothing records the STATE the caller saw, when it saw it, or that it looked again after being refused. WHY THIS IS NOT ENFORCED_AT_SURFACE_ONLY, though there is a genuine near-miss I want on the record rather than suppressed: apps/rph-demo/src/lib/server/authoring-turn-machine.ts:43 declares `CONFLICTED: { on: { DISCARD: 'DISCARDED' } }` — a conflicted authoring turn has NO edge back to COMMITTING, so the only way forward is DISCARD and a NEW turn, and a new turn re-runs `snapshotRevisions` at turn start. That structurally forces reload-and-re-form, and the sibling COMMIT_FAILED state carries the explicit docblock "Do not expose blind retry; inspect/reconcile or discard this in-process candidate." But it binds exactly one flow (the PWA authoring turn, whose sole production entry is `commitAuthoringTurn` in apps/rph-demo/src/lib/server/authoring-turn.ts), it is above the seam, and it says nothing about the other 27 dispatch sites, the test-api endpoint, or any direct Engine.dispatch caller — all of which I drove and all of which admit the blind retry. Claiming the surface arm on the strength of one machine would be the ASR-3 error with a different mask. THE ONE RATIFIED SHAPE THAT WOULD CARRY THIS EXISTS ONLY AS TEXT: JPWB-SPEC-001 §11.4.22 FORK-22 item 2 requires a Projection to record `derivedAtSubjectRevision` and a `freshness` state, and REG-F-050 identifies that value precisely — "a caller-side value captured when the projection was derived — the revision the professional believed current. That is PER-4's phrase performed, and it is the one value an engine cannot fabricate." It has zero implementation (census below), and REG-F-050 is still Status: OPEN.
missing_shape: There is no field, command or event anywhere that records what state a caller READ before issuing, so nothing can be compared against a re-issue. Concretely absent, all four verified by census C3: (1) no read-provenance field on the DomainCommand envelope — `expectedRevision` asserts a NUMBER, not a READ, and nothing records when or from what the caller obtained it; (2) `derivedAtSubjectRevision` — the caller-side value SPEC-001 §11.4.22 item 2 ratifies for exactly this purpose — has ZERO occurrences repository-wide; (3) no Projection `freshness` state exists, so nothing can even mark a caller's basis as STALE; (4) no read-receipt, read-token or reload event exists, so a reload leaves no trace an engine could require. Consequently there is also no `SPEC-001-FX-FRESH-18` check to be dead: the predicate is not dead, it was never expressible.

owed: A REG-F FINDING IS OWED, AND IT IS A NARROW ONE — the general concurrency gap is already filed twice (RPH-CON-003, REG-F-050), but NEITHER filing states THIS claim. RPH-CON-003 is about the declaration being absent; REG-F-050 is about who supplies the number and about the surface obligation. What neither records is that a caller which HAS a number and never reloaded is indistinguishable, in the governed stream, from one that reloaded and re-decided — i.e. that PER-4's second clause has no carrier at all in the record, only in the two callers' heads. The filing should name: (a) the driven arrangement and its control (blind bump vs reload+re-form producing identical streams [0,1,2]); (b) that the one ratified shape which would carry it, SPEC-001 §11.4.22's `derivedAtSubjectRevision`, is at zero implementation and its parent finding REG-F-050 is OPEN; (c) that apps/rph-demo/src/lib/server/authoring-turn-machine.ts:43 is the only site in the repository that structurally forces the remedy, so it is the precedent a general answer should generalise from rather than a coverage claim. I also record, against the split rule w3b-limb-split/1.0.0 rather than against the repository: this is the one limb of the five whose SUBJECT is not the system, and the arm set has no vocabulary for "the obligation is real, the engine is the wrong addressee, and the repository has exactly one site that discharges it". UNENFORCED_NO_SHAPE is the honest fit but reads as a flat absence, which understates authoring-turn-machine.ts:43.

evidence: THE LIMB IS CONJUNCTIVE AND THE TWO CONJUNCTS COME OUT DIFFERENTLY, so I measured both rather than reporting one and inferring the other. CONJUNCT (b) — "never silently retries with stale business assumptions" — HOLDS, and it holds by there being no automatic retry to be silent. Censused the entire command path (packages/rph-application/src/command-bus.ts, packages/rph-engine/src/*.ts, apps/rph-demo/src/lib/server/*.ts): every occurrence of retry/retries/retrying is one of three things and none of them is an automatic re-dispatch — (i) a HUMAN-INITIATED xstate event (`BLOCKED_EXTERNAL: { on: { RETRY_ASSURANCE: 'ASSURING' } }`), (ii) prose/UI advice (`floor.ts` RETRY_OR_CONFIGURE_REVIEWER, STALE_FORM's "Reload the page and retry"), or (iii) an explicit REFUSAL to retry, which is the cited site: apps/rph-demo/src/lib/server/authoring-turn-machine.ts:45 reads "A transport/process failure cannot distinguish 'definitely not committed' from unknown success without a durable change-set receipt. Do not expose blind retry; inspect/reconcile or discard this in-process candidate.", and the machine performs it — CONFLICTED and COMMIT_FAILED both have exactly one outgoing edge, DISCARD. In the domain proper, a retry is a first-class governed COMMAND, not a loop: `retryExecutionStep` (packages/rph-application/src/handlers/execution.ts:1505) is dispatched by an actor, gated by `stepAuthorityRefusal` (plan-ACTIVE per RPH-EXE-002, the `retryDecision` cap per RPH-EXE-008, and a refusal when the last failure class does not permit RETRY), loads CURRENT state through `loadOrReject`, and emits its own event — so it is neither silent nor operating on stale assumptions. Even PER-5 replay is not a retry in this sense: a repeated idempotency key returns the PRIOR result rather than re-executing. CONJUNCT (a) — "never silently overwrites" — DIVERGES, and I drove the full two-actor arrangement rather than a lone omission: caller A read the INTENT at revision 0; a concurrent writer advanced it to 1; caller A wrote with `expectedRevision` absent from the envelope. ACCEPTED, aggregate 1 -> 2, and caller A was told nothing — no CONFLICT, no warning, no signal of any kind that the state it acted on had moved underneath it. That is last-write-wins between concurrent actors, which is exactly what canon's WHY names ("last-write-wins on governed state is unrecorded authority transfer between concurrent actors"). It is worth being precise about "silently", because an event IS appended and the append-only log does record THAT the write happened: what is silent is the TRANSFER — nothing records that caller A's decision rested on a superseded read, and neither actor is informed. THE DIVERGENCE IS PARTLY FENCED, which is why this is PARTIAL and not a flat unenforced: on the authoring-turn path `commitGuardPreconditions` (apps/rph-demo/src/lib/server/authoring-turn.ts:401-418) makes the guard vector total over every touched aggregate — `expectedRevision` from the turn-start snapshot, or `mustNotExist`, with no third arm — and command-bus.ts:554 `if (actualRevision !== expectedRevision)` refuses the batch as `guardConflict`, which `recordCommitFailure` turns into the CONFLICTED state that cannot retry. On the 15 form-round-trip route actions the rendered revision fail-closes. On the remainder — undertakings/[id]/+page.server.ts:672, routes/+page.server.ts:45, and any direct dispatcher — the silent overwrite is the default.

sibling_control: TWO SEPARATIONS WERE NEEDED HERE. FIRST, against limb 1: limb 1 says the CALLER must declare; limb 4(a) says the SYSTEM must not silently overwrite. Same root mechanism, different claims and different addressees — a system could satisfy limb 4(a) with no declaration at all (e.g. by refusing any write whose loaded revision differs from a recorded read), and could satisfy limb 1 while still overwriting if the declaration were unchecked. I am reporting them as two divergences with one cause, not the same row twice, and the ENFORCED conjunct (b) is what makes this row's content distinct. SECOND, on the cited site: authoring-turn-machine.ts:45 refuses, in its own terms, "a turn that reached CONFLICTED or COMMIT_FAILED being re-committed" — the machine gives those two states exactly one outgoing edge, DISCARD.
